patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Airtable and Linear share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Airtable only if your buying job matches “Flexible database / app platform with interfaces and light project apps — Team from ~$20/u” rather than Linear's shape. Choose Linear only if your buying job matches “Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo ” rather than Airtable's shape. Workflow advantage differs because Airtable is shaped for Flexible database / app platform with interfaces and light project app whereas Linear is shaped for Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Bas. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Airtable and Linear share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Airtable is Flexible database / app platform with interfaces and light project apps — Team from ~$20/user/mo annual.; Linear is Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Airtable (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Linear (startup, small-business, mid-market).
- Researched limits: Airtable — Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp; Linear — Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS.

Limitations — Airtable: Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp; Builder complexity; Linear: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Leaner automation than Jira Enterprise.

Poor-fit cases: Airtable is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp · Linear is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS · Avoid Airtable if you actually need Linear's motion (Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
